name: Jayden Daniels

background.fact: Born December 18, 2000 in Fontana, California and raised in nearby San Bernardino; he played at Cajon High School, setting California Interscholastic Federation Southern Section records with 210 touchdowns and over 17,600 total yards in 53 games.
He played three seasons at Arizona State and two at LSU; at LSU in 2023 he won the Heisman Trophy after leading the FBS in total yards and setting the single season passer rating record.

Washington drafted him second overall in 2024; he set several rookie records, led the Commanders to their most wins in a season and first NFC Championship Game since 1991, and was named Offensive Rookie of the Year.
His walk-off Hail Mary touchdown pass in 2024, known as the Hail Maryland, was named the season's Moment of the Year.
Listed at 6 ft 4 in, 210 lb, age 25, jersey 5, third NFL season, depth chart QB1.
background.source: research/data/TUR-QB.json (bio, from ESPN and Sleeper pulls)

background.fact: Described as a dual-threat quarterback with a drop-back passer's accuracy and field awareness plus the speed to scramble; known for composure in late-game moments. He warms up with a basketball, a routine learned from childhood friend C. J. Stroud.

family.fact: His father Javon Daniels played college cornerback at Washington and Iowa State; his mother Regina Jackson works as his business manager and agent; he has an older sister, Bianca.
His mother Regina was among those who posted public comments when ABC named Washington backup Sam Hartman the new Bachelor (headline only seen; article text not read).

His maternal great-grandmother emigrated from Japan; Wikipedia calls him the first starting NFL quarterback with Japanese ancestry since 1928. He earned a business communications degree from Arizona State in December 2021. No spouse or children found: not found.

scouts_read: Daniels is active and had a full week of practice before the Giants game, and he now gets 11 days to rest before Cincinnati. The elbow kept him out of two games earlier this year, so a setback is the main thing to watch, but nothing is reported for Week 11 yet. The Monday night total is above 51, which suggests Washington will have to throw to keep pace with Burrow. His rushing has been modest, so his floor depends on touchdown passes to Diggs and Williams. I would project a decent game near 20 points with a real chance of a big one if the game turns into a shootout.
